name: The Freelance Desk
who: Owners of 5–25 person businesses who now depend on three or four freelancers — a designer, a copywriter, a developer, a bookkeeper — and are managing all of them personally.
problem: "I've got five freelancers and I'm the only one who knows what each of them is doing. When one disappears mid-project it's my evening that goes. I'd rather manage one relationship than five."
solution: We become the single point of contact. We source and vet the freelancers the business needs, write the briefs, check the work before it lands, and keep a bench so a disappearance is a phone call rather than a crisis.
promise: Five freelancers, and you are the only person who knows what each of them is doing. One relationship instead of five: we source, brief and manage them, and cover you when one drops out.
gets:
Sourcing and vetting for each role you need filled
Briefs written and work checked before it reaches you
A named backup for every role, so nothing stops when someone disappears
positioning: A marketplace hands over a list. This hands over one contact and keeps the continuity — which is the part the owner is actually paying for.
voice: Steady and accountable. Talks about who is doing what by when.
channels: Existing freelance network, LinkedIn, agencies with overflow, referral from current clients
